name: C3 Glomerulonephritis

criteria.description: Renal biopsy showing dominant C3 deposition with minimal or no immunoglobulin deposits on immunofluorescence
Evidence of alternative complement pathway dysregulation (e.g., low serum C3, presence of C3 nephritic factor)
Exclusion of other causes of glomerulonephritis such as post-infectious GN or immune complex GN
Presentation with hematuria, proteinuria, or renal impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Renal biopsy demonstrating dominant C3 deposition with minimal immunoglobulins plus evidence of alternative complement pathway dysregulation and exclusion of other glomerulonephritides
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on renal biopsy and complement studies; genetic testing may support diagnosis.

laboratory: Low serum C3 with normal C4 levels
Presence of C3 nephritic factor (autoantibody stabilizing C3 convertase)
Elevated serum creatinine in advanced disease
imaging: Renal ultrasound may show normal or increased echogenicity
No specific imaging findings diagnostic for C3GN
other: Renal biopsy immunofluorescence showing dominant C3 deposits with minimal immunoglobulins
Electron microscopy showing electron-dense deposits in the glomerular basement membrane or mesangium

distinguishingFeatures: Usually follows infection with latent period
Presence of immunoglobulin deposits along with C3
Typically self-limited with normalization of complement
Electron microscopy shows dense ribbon-like deposits in glomerular basement membrane
Also a form of C3 glomerulopathy but distinct ultrastructural features
